items.title: Exact potential-wave multiplier identity

references.title: Mihalis Dafermos and Igor Rodnianski, Lectures on black holes and linear waves, arXiv:0811.0354v1 (2008), full lecture notes
references.locator: Appendix D, PDF pp. 103–104, derives the massless scalar stress-current divergence identity; Sections 3.2.2–3.2.4, PDF pp. 30–32, apply it to energy flux and identify horizon degeneration. The potential and source terms below are calculated locally.

references.title: Elena Giorgi, The linear stability of Reissner–Nordström spacetime for small charge, arXiv:1904.04926v2 (2020), full paper
references.locator: Section 1.2, PDF pp. 3–6, and Sections 8.1.2 and 8.4, PDF pp. 56–60: coupled wave systems in the Einstein–Maxwell application. The scalar identity below is proved directly and is not used as a substitute for those systems.

items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$, $\mathcal U$, $u$, $V$, $s$, and $X$ satisfy the data and definitions of the wave-current definition, including $\Box_g u=Vu+s$. Then
$$\nabla_aJ_X^a=K_X+sX(u)-\frac12X(V)u^2.$$
In particular, if $X$ satisfies the Killing equation $\nabla_{(a}X_{b)}=0$, $X(V)=0$, and $s=0$, then $\nabla_aJ_X^a=0$. At a point where $n$ is a future unit timelike vector and $X$ is timelike with $-g(X,n)>0$, the density $T_{ab}X^a n^b$ is nonnegative whenever $V\ge0$.

items.title: Positive matrix-potential wave system energy

references.title: Mihalis Dafermos and Igor Rodnianski, Lectures on black holes and linear waves, arXiv:0811.0354v1 (2008), full lecture notes
references.locator: Appendix D, PDF pp. 103–104, and Section 3.2.2, PDF pp. 30–31, use scalar multiplier currents and flux identities. The finite-dimensional matrix-potential estimate here is proved locally by summing scalar identities and cancelling the symmetric off-diagonal terms.

references.title: Elena Giorgi, The linear stability of Reissner–Nordström spacetime for small charge, arXiv:1904.04926v2 (2020), full paper
references.locator: Section 1.2, PDF pp. 3–6, and Sections 8.1.2 and 8.4, PDF pp. 56–60, exhibit the extra structure in actual coupled Einstein–Maxwell wave systems. This theorem assumes an abstract symmetric nonnegative potential and does not assert that those fields satisfy its hypotheses.

items.statement:
Let $N\ge1$, $I:=[0,T)$ with $0<T\le\infty$, and let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $I$. Let $U,S\in C^\infty(J\times\mathbb R,\mathbb R^N)$. Write $\operatorname{Sym}_N(\mathbb R)$ for the real symmetric $N\times N$ matrices and use the Euclidean dot product and norm on $\mathbb R^N$. Let $V\in C^\infty(\mathbb R,\operatorname{Sym}_N(\mathbb R))$ be bounded, independent of $t$, and positive semidefinite at every $x$, meaning $z^{\mathsf T}V(x)z\ge0$ for every $z\in\mathbb R^N$. Assume $U$ and all its mixed derivatives of total order at most two, and $S$, are Schwartz in $x$ locally uniformly for $t\in J$: for every compact $K\subset J$, every such derivative $D$ and every integer $m\ge0$, $\sup_{t\in K,x\in\mathbb R}(1+|x|)^m|DU(t,x)|<\infty$, and the analogous bounds hold for $S$. If
$$U_{tt}-U_{xx}+V(x)U=S,$$
define
$$E(t):=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(|U_t|^2+|U_x|^2+U^{\mathsf T}V(x)U\bigr)\,dx,$$
where $|\cdot|$ is the Euclidean norm and $\|v(t,\cdot)\|_2^2:=\int_{\mathbb R}|v(t,x)|^2\,dx$ for any vector-valued function $v$. Then $E(t)\ge0$,
$$E'(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}U_t\cdot S\,dx,\qquad\sqrt{E(t)}\le\sqrt{E(0)}+\frac1{\sqrt2}\int_0^t\|S(\tau,\cdot)\|_2\,d\tau\quad(t\in I).$$
In particular $E$ is constant when $S=0$. If $t,x$ have length units and $U$ has unit $[U]$, then $V$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-2}$, $S$ has unit $[U]\mathrm m^{-2}$, $E$ has unit $[U]^2\mathrm m^{-1}$, and both sides of the square-root estimate have unit $[U]\mathrm m^{-1/2}$. This abstract estimate supplies neither pointwise decay nor a reconstruction of coupled Einstein–Maxwell perturbations.

items.title: Subextremal RN scalar mode potential and conditional energy

references.title: Mihalis Dafermos and Igor Rodnianski, Lectures on black holes and linear waves, arXiv:0811.0354v1 (2008), full lecture notes
references.locator: Sections 3.2.2–3.2.4 and Appendix F.2, PDF pp. 30–32 and 105–106: scalar-wave Killing currents, horizon degeneration and the Schwarzschild separated radial equation. The exact charged RN reduction below is computed directly from the local RN metric.

references.title: Elena Giorgi, The linear stability of Reissner–Nordström spacetime for small charge, arXiv:1904.04926v2 (2020), full paper
references.locator: Sections 1.2–1.3 and 8.1.2–8.4, PDF pp. 3–6 and 56–60: the coupled Einstein–Maxwell master systems, transformations and low-mode distinctions. Those results are not used to identify the scalar test equation with a coupled perturbation system.

items.statement:
Let $m>0$ and $q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$ be length parameters, put $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2$, and assume $Q^2<m^2$. Define
$$r_\pm:=m\pm\sqrt{m^2-Q^2},\qquad f(r):=1-\frac{2m}{r}+\frac{Q^2}{r^2}\quad(r>0).$$
On the fixed exterior $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ext}}=\mathbb R_t\times(r_+,\infty)_r\times S^2$, use the exact dyonic Reissner–Nordström metric specified by the preceding mathematical definition with its mass parameter identified as $M=m$ and charges $q_e,q_m$, and set $t=x^0$. Define a real normalized spherical harmonic of degree $\ell\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ to mean a smooth real $Y:S^2\to\mathbb R$ such that
$$\int_{S^2}Y^2\,d\omega_{S^2}=1,\qquad \Delta_{\gamma_{S^2}}Y=-\ell(\ell+1)Y,$$
where in the standard polar chart
$$\Delta_{\gamma_{S^2}}Y=\frac1{\sin\theta}\partial_\theta(\sin\theta\,\partial_\theta Y)+\frac1{\sin^2\theta}\partial_\phi^2Y.$$
Here $d\omega_{S^2}$ is the area measure of the unit round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$, and $f'(r)$ denotes the ordinary derivative of $f$ with respect to $r$. Since $r_+>0$, the basepoint $r_0:=2r_+$ lies in the exterior; define the tortoise coordinate by the oriented integral $r_*(r):=\int_{r_0}^{r}f(\rho)^{-1}\,d\rho$. For any such $Y$, let $\psi(t,r,\omega)=\phi(t,r)Y(\omega)$ be a smooth real solution of $\Box_g\psi=0$, and put $U_\ell(t,r_*):=r\phi(t,r)$. Then $r_*$ is a smooth coordinate from $(r_+,\infty)$ onto $\mathbb R$, and
$$\partial_t^2U_\ell-\partial_{r_*}^2U_\ell+V_\ell(r_*)U_\ell=0,\qquad V_\ell(r_*):=f(r)\left(\frac{\ell(\ell+1)}{r^2}+\frac{f'(r)}r\right).$$
The potential is smooth, bounded, and strictly positive on $\mathbb R$. If $U_\ell$ and its derivatives satisfy the decay assumptions of the positive matrix-potential wave-energy theorem on the time interval considered, then
$$E_\ell(t):=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R}\left((\partial_tU_\ell)^2+(\partial_{r_*}U_\ell)^2+V_\ell U_\ell^2\right)\,dr_*$$
is constant there. In the original radial coordinate, its radial derivative term is $\frac12\int_{r_+}^{\infty}f(r)|\partial_rU_\ell|^2\,dr$; this energy loses control of $\partial_rU_\ell$ as $r\downarrow r_+$. It asserts no nondegenerate horizon-crossing derivative estimate, decay estimate, or coupled Einstein–Maxwell stability result. The coordinates $t,r,r_*$ and parameters $m,q_e,q_m$ have unit metres, $f$ is dimensionless, and $V_\ell$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-2}$. If $\psi,\phi$ have a common arbitrary field unit $\Phi$, then $Y$ is dimensionless, $U_\ell$ has unit $\Phi\,\mathrm m$, and $E_\ell$ has unit $\Phi^2\,\mathrm m$.

items.title: An explicit conditional nonlinear energy closure

references.title: Mihalis Dafermos and Igor Rodnianski, Lectures on black holes and linear waves, arXiv:0811.0354v1 (2008), full lecture notes
references.locator: Sections 5.2.6 and 7.1, PDF pp. 68–69 and 86–87, place energy estimates inside explicit bootstrap and non-extremal redshift hypotheses. The scalar ODE implication and its exact coefficient threshold are proved locally here.

references.title: Elena Giorgi, The linear stability of Reissner–Nordström spacetime for small charge, arXiv:1904.04926v2 (2020), full paper
references.locator: Sections 1.2–1.4 and 7, PDF pp. 3–7 and 55–56, state the exact transformed systems, small-charge hypotheses, gauge conditions and reconstruction used for the full linear result. The present proposition is only an ODE implication and does not inherit that theorem.

items.statement:
Let $I=[0,T)$ with $0<T\le\infty$, and let $E:I\to[0,\infty)$ be the energy functional of a wave system of the kind specified in the preceding positive matrix-potential energy theorem, restricted to its existence interval. Here absolute continuity on compact subintervals has the endpoint-increment meaning in the cited definition. Suppose $E$ is absolutely continuous on every compact subinterval of $I$ and, for constants $C\ge0$, $\delta>0$, satisfies for almost every $t\in I$
$$E'(t)\le C(1+t)^{-1-\delta}E(t)^{3/2}.$$
If $E(0)>0$ and $C\sqrt{E(0)}<2\delta$, then
$$E(t)\le E(0)\left[1-\frac{C\sqrt{E(0)}}{2\delta}\right]^{-2}\qquad(t\in I).$$
This is a bound only on the given existence interval; a separate continuation theorem is needed to infer global existence. For comparison, if $C>0$ and the coefficient is changed to $(1+t)^{-1}$, the equality model $E'=C(1+t)^{-1}E^{3/2}$ with the same positive initial value blows up at the finite time $\exp(2/(C\sqrt{E(0)}))-1$. This comparison is an ODE example, not a claim that an RN or Kerr–Newman perturbation satisfies either differential inequality. Time and energy are dimensionless in this scalar comparison.
